newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - German shares lead Euro-bourses into retreat.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - German shares lead Euro-bourses into retreat.

text.p: European stocks and bond markets went into retreat on Thursday after investors sold Wall Street down and inflation worries injected fresh nervousness into U.S. Treasuries.
Frankfurt led Europe's major bourses down, falling more than two percent at the opening of floor trade. London and Paris also dropped but the falls were nowhere as bad.

On the currency front, the dollar opened below 1.70 marks for the first time in almost two weeks, pressured by a benign assessment of U.S. inflationary prospects in the Federal Reserve's Beige Book report on Wednesday and renewed firmness in the the mark and Swiss franc.

"There seems to be a generalised push back to marks and Swiss francs and as the Beige Book really gave us no strong view on the chances for rate rise...the dollar's suffered," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN Amro.
By 1015 GMT the dollar was trading at 1.6949 marks and 122.32 yen, compared with 1.7023 marks and 122.62 yen in late trading on Wednesday.

A selloff in high technology stocks and bonds was mainly behind the 45 point fall in the Dow Jones Industrial Average to 7,039 points overnight, which followed two consecutive record highs. Financial and pharmaceutical stocks, which have posted the sharpest rallies this year, also suffered.
Analysts said investors had become unwilling to broaden stock selections beyond mainly defensive blue-chip issues, undermining the wide rally that had driven the market in recent months.

Although the Fed's Beige Book showed price pressures under control, the U.S. bond market remained nervous about inflation -- reflected in early weakness in the British and German government bond markets.

That added to selling pressures in equity markets, although traders cited Wall Street's performance as the major factor in declining share prices that also saw Tokyo's Nikkei index shed 1.56 percent over the day.
They said share and bond markets were likely to focus on U.S. retail sales data, due at 1330 GMT, for signs of whether a robust U.S. economy could prompt a near-term Federal Reserve rate hike.
The early two percent fall in German bourse trade was blamed on the market catching up with Wednesday's losses in IBIS screen-based business, Wall Street and the drop in the dollar.

Commerzbank led the losers, falling 1.95 marks to 44.95 marks in active dealings. Hoechst tumbled for the third day on disappointment that it was dropping a plan to list its HMR drugs unit. It was down 1.60 marks, or 2.2 percent, at 68.85 by 1000 GMT.
Some traders said the drop may be the start of a long-awaited correction in response to the sharp gains posted by the DAX index in recent weeks.
But others said the market was merely following the lead of Wall Street and that most of the selling and trading volumes were concentrated in the chemical sector.
Traders in London said the FTSE 100 index's early losses echoed similar falls on Wednesday, although they did not expect a significant pull-back.
"We're just seeing a mirror image of yesterday. The Dow had a bad day so the market makers push prices down a bit but so far there aren't too many sellers," one senior trader said.
The FTSE 100 index was down about 0.4 percent at 4,404.
It was a similar story in Paris, where French shares shed 0.88 percent before quickly finding sufficient support to cut back losses.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 17.9 points, or 0.68 percent at 2,623.8 by about 1015 GMT.
On foreign exchange markets analysts said a generalised paring of high-yield currency positions in Europe was tending to boost lower-yield currencies, benefiting the Swiss franc.

Despite renewed assurances from Wednesday's Franco-German summit meeting about economic and moneatry union (EMU) in Europe, the market continued to appear nervous about a possible delay in the project.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6949 marks and 122.32 yen, compared with 1.7023 marks and 122.62 yen in late trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1015 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 17.6 points, or 0.4 percent, at 4,404.9.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 17.9, or 0.68 percent, at 2,623.8.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 67.4 points, or 1.97 percent, at 3,348.0.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $351.45 up five cents. Palladium fell $3.00 from $152.75, while silver was down a cent at $5.23.
